</td><td>

Fixed-rate offer-chain parameters without a side field.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

readonly [FixedRateOfferChainLeg](#midnight-sdk.fixedrateofferchainleg)<!-- -->\[\]

Lend-side offer legs that can be mapped to `Offer.create({ buy: true, ... })`<!-- -->.

## Exceptions

`InvalidOfferParameterError` when an input is invalid or the end timestamp exceeds the supported horizon.

## Remarks

Parameter details:

- `params.targetRate`<!-- -->: Target yearly fixed rate expressed as a decimal number.

- `params.tickSpacing`<!-- -->: Tick spacing enforced by the market.

- `params.maturityTimestamp`<!-- -->: Market maturity timestamp in seconds.

- `params.chainStartTimestamp`<!-- -->: First timestamp the chain should cover.

- `params.chainEndTimestamp`<!-- -->: Latest timestamp the chain may cover.

## Example


```ts
import { Offer, OfferChainUtils } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";

const legs = OfferChainUtils.buildLendFixedRateOfferChain({
  targetRate: 0.05,
  tickSpacing: market.tickSpacing,
  maturityTimestamp: market.params.maturity,
  chainStartTimestamp: now,
  chainEndTimestamp: expiry,
});
const offers = legs.map((leg) =>
  Offer.create({
    ...baseOffer,
    buy: true,
    tick: leg.tick,
    start: leg.startTimestamp,
    expiry: leg.expiryTimestamp,
  }),
);
```

<a name="midnight-sdk.offerchainutils.getmaxfixedrateofferchainendtimestamp"></a>

## OfferChainUtils.getMaxFixedRateOfferChainEndTimestamp() function

Returns the latest supported end timestamp for a fixed-rate offer chain.

Chains intentionally stop before the final part of the maturity window because rate sensitivity accelerates near maturity and would require too many short-lived offers for a stable maker quote. Call this when constraining a make-offer expiry selector, then pass the selected timestamp to the lend-only or borrow-only chain builder.

**Signature:**

```typescript
function getMaxFixedRateOfferChainEndTimestamp(params: {
        readonly maturityTimestamp: BigIntish;
        readonly chainStartTimestamp: BigIntish;
    }): bigint;
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

params


</td><td>

{ readonly maturityTimestamp: [BigIntish](./morpho-ts.md#morpho-ts.bigintish)<!-- -->; readonly chainStartTimestamp: [BigIntish](./morpho-ts.md#morpho-ts.bigintish)<!-- -->; }


</td><td>

Maturity and chain-start timestamps.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

bigint

Latest accepted chain end timestamp.

## Exceptions

`InvalidOfferParameterError` when a timestamp is invalid.

## Remarks

Parameter details:

- `params.maturityTimestamp`<!-- -->: Market maturity timestamp in seconds.

- `params.chainStartTimestamp`<!-- -->: First timestamp the chain should cover.

## Example


```ts
import { OfferChainUtils } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";

const maxExpiry = OfferChainUtils.getMaxFixedRateOfferChainEndTimestamp({
  maturityTimestamp: market.params.maturity,
  chainStartTimestamp: now,
});
console.log(maxExpiry);
```

<a name="midnight-sdk.offerstruct"></a>

## OfferStruct interface

ABI tuple shape for `Offer`<!-- -->.

This is the shape consumed by viem encoders, Merkle leaf hashing, payload encoding, and take calldata encoders. Build it with `OfferUtils.toStruct` or `GroupUtils.toStructs`<!-- -->; grouped encoders derive a shared group id from the offer list, while single-offer encoders read the offer's group unless an explicit override is supplied.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export interface OfferStruct
```

## Example


```ts
import type { OfferStruct } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";
import { zeroAddress, zeroHash } from "viem";

const offer: OfferStruct = {
  market: {
    chainId: 8453,
    midnight: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001000",
    loanToken: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000006000",
    collateralParams: [
      {
        token: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000007000",
        lltv: 770000000000000000n,
        liquidationCursor: 250000000000000000n,
        oracle: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000008000",
      },
    ],
    maturity: 2_000n,
    rcfThreshold: 0n,
    enterGate: zeroAddress,
    liquidatorGate: zeroAddress,
  },
  buy: true,
  maker: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000009000",
  start: 0n,
  expiry: 2_100n,
  tick: 5_000n,
  group: zeroHash,
  callback: zeroAddress,
  callbackData: "0x",
```

<a name="midnight-sdk.offerutils"></a>

## OfferUtils namespace

Object-compatible helpers for Midnight offer construction, grouping, and take-side encoding.

Make-side apps usually call [Offer.create()](#midnight-sdk.offer.create)<!-- -->, then `Group.create` or `Tree.create`<!-- -->. Use these helpers when you need the same validation or ABI conversion without depending on class instances, or when converting API data into the structs consumed by payload and take encoders.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export declare namespace OfferUtils
```

## Example


```ts
import { OfferUtils } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";

console.log(typeof OfferUtils.getOfferExpiry);
```

## Functions

Function


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>

[getApr(params)](#midnight-sdk.offerutils.getapr)

It computes time to maturity from the offer market and delegates the final tick annualization to `TickLib.tickToApr`<!-- -->.

<tr><td>

</td><td>

The rate is the offer's fixed period rate divided by the market's remaining time to maturity at `timestamp`<!-- -->, rounded up.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[groupHash(offer)](#midnight-sdk.offerutils.grouphash)


</td><td>

Computes the offer hash used to derive a content-addressed group id.

The encoded group is always the protocol zero hash. Use this only for standalone or grouped-offer id derivation, not for final tree leaves or payload offers.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[hash(offer)](#midnight-sdk.offerutils.hash)


</td><td>

Computes the canonical protocol offer hash from the offer's group id.

Use this for final tree leaves and payload offers after a group has been assigned. Use `groupHash` for the zero-group hash that derives a group id.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[hashStruct(offerStruct)](#midnight-sdk.offerutils.hashstruct)


</td><td>

Computes the canonical protocol offer hash for an ABI-compatible offer.

Use when you already have an `OfferStruct`<!-- -->, for example from `GroupUtils.toStructs`<!-- -->, `TreeUtils.buildDescriptor`<!-- -->, or decoded payload bytes. Use `hash` when you still have a grouped `Offer` or grouped plain offer input, and `groupHash` when deriving a group id from the zero-group hash.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[resolveReceiverIfMakerIsSeller(params)](#midnight-sdk.offerutils.resolvereceiverifmakerisseller)


</td><td>

Resolves and validates the maker-seller receiver field for an offer side.

Use this before `Offer.create` when side-specific receiver defaults must be displayed to a maker. `Offer.create` calls it internally.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[toStruct(params)](#midnight-sdk.offerutils.tostruct)


</td><td>

Converts an offer into the tuple object expected by viem ABI encoders.

This is the bridge from SDK/domain objects into Merkle leaf hashing, payload items, and take calldata encoding.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[validateContinuousFeeCap(params)](#midnight-sdk.offerutils.validatecontinuousfeecap)


</td><td>

Validates and normalizes the maximum continuous fee an offer accepts.

Use this before `Offer.create` when a maker UI exposes fee tolerance. `Offer.create` calls it internally and defaults omitted values to zero so fresh offers fail closed unless the maker explicitly accepts a fee cap.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[validateOfferCaps(params)](#midnight-sdk.offerutils.validateoffercaps)


</td><td>

Validates and normalizes mutually exclusive offer caps.

Use this before `Offer.create` when a UI lets makers choose between a unit cap and an asset cap. `Offer.create` calls it internally.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[validateOfferGroup(params)](#midnight-sdk.offerutils.validateoffergroup)


</td><td>

Validates protocol-level mechanics for one Midnight offer consumption group.

Use before deriving a content-addressed group id. Grouped offers must share maker, side, loan token, cap mode, and cap value because Midnight tracks one consumed scalar per maker and group. `Group.create` calls this automatically; call it directly only when you need the normalized offers without constructing a `Group`<!-- -->.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[validateOfferParams(params)](#midnight-sdk.offerutils.validateofferparams)


</td><td>

Validates deterministic make-offer parameters without constructing an offer.

Use when an app needs normalized maker input or field-level errors before instantiating an `Offer`<!-- -->. `Offer.create` uses the same validation and then constructs the class instance for grouping and trees.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[validateOfferTick(params)](#midnight-sdk.offerutils.validateoffertick)


</td><td>

Validates and normalizes a Midnight offer tick and spacing.

Use this for form-level validation before `Offer.create` when you want to surface a tick-specific issue. `Offer.create` calls it internally.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[validateOfferTimeRange(params)](#midnight-sdk.offerutils.validateoffertimerange)


</td><td>

Validates and normalizes an offer start/expiry range.

Use this before `Offer.create` when a UI edits dates separately from other offer fields. `Offer.create` calls it internally.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

<a name="midnight-sdk.offerutils.getapr"></a>

## OfferUtils.getApr() function

Converts an offer tick into a WAD simple annual percentage rate at a timestamp.

It computes time to maturity from the offer market and delegates the final tick annualization to `TickLib.tickToApr`<!-- -->.

**Signature:**

```typescript
function getApr(params: {
        readonly offer: Pick<IOffer, "market" | "tick">;
        readonly timestamp: BigIntish;
    }): bigint;
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

params


</td><td>

{ readonly offer: Pick&lt;[IOffer](#midnight-sdk.ioffer)<!-- -->, "market" \| "tick"&gt;; readonly timestamp: [BigIntish](./morpho-ts.md#morpho-ts.bigintish)<!-- -->; }


</td><td>


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

bigint

WAD simple APR rounded up.

## Exceptions

`NegativeValueError` when `market.maturity`<!-- -->, `timestamp`<!-- -->, or `tick` is negative.

`TickOutOfRangeError` when `tick` exceeds `MAX_TICK`<!-- -->.

`DivisionByZeroError` when the tick price is zero or `timestamp` is at or after maturity.

## Remarks

Parameter details:

- `params.offer`<!-- -->: Offer to inspect.

- `params.timestamp`<!-- -->: Timestamp at which the APR is calculated.

## Example


```ts
import { Offer, OfferUtils } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";

const offer = Offer.from({
  market: {
    loanToken: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000006000",
    collateralParams: [
      {
        token: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000007000",
        lltv: 770000000000000000n,
        liquidationCursor: 250000000000000000n,
        oracle: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000008000",
      },
    ],
    maturity: 54_000n,
    rcfThreshold: 0n,
    enterGate: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000",
    liquidatorGate: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000",
  },
  buy: true,
  maker: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000009000",
  start: 0n,
  expiry: 3_600n,
  tick: 5_000n,
  callback: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000",
  callbackData: "0x",
  receiverIfMakerIsSeller: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000",
  ratifier: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000004000",
  reduceOnly: false,
  maxUnits: 100n,
  maxAssets: 0n,
  continuousFeeCap: 317097919n,
});
const apr = OfferUtils.getApr({ offer, timestamp: 1_000n });
console.log(apr);
```

<a name="midnight-sdk.offerutils.getconsumableunits"></a>

## OfferUtils.getConsumableUnits() function

Returns remaining units accepted by an offer's cap at a timestamp.

The offer must carry a hydrated [Market](#midnight-sdk.market) so the current market continuous fee and settlement-fee buckets are available locally. Fetch the current `consumed(maker, group)` value separately and pass it as input.

**Signature:**

```typescript
function getConsumableUnits(params: {
        readonly offer: Pick<IOffer, "market" | "buy" | "start" | "expiry" | "tick" | "maxUnits" | "maxAssets" | "continuousFeeCap">;
        readonly consumed: BigIntish;
        readonly timestamp: BigIntish;
    }): bigint;
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

params


</td><td>

{ readonly offer: Pick&lt;[IOffer](#midnight-sdk.ioffer)<!-- -->, "market" \| "buy" \| "start" \| "expiry" \| "tick" \| "maxUnits" \| "maxAssets" \| "continuousFeeCap"&gt;; readonly consumed: [BigIntish](./morpho-ts.md#morpho-ts.bigintish)<!-- -->; readonly timestamp: [BigIntish](./morpho-ts.md#morpho-ts.bigintish)<!-- -->; }


</td><td>


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

bigint

Remaining consumable units accepted by Midnight `take`<!-- -->.

## Exceptions

`InvalidOfferParameterError` when the offer does not carry hydrated market state or has invalid caps.

`NegativeValueError` when `consumed`<!-- -->, `timestamp`<!-- -->, offer limits, or delegated math inputs are negative.

`TickOutOfRangeError` when `tick` exceeds `MAX_TICK`<!-- -->.

`SettlementFeeExceedsPriceError` when settlement fee exceeds a buy-offer price.

## Remarks

Parameter details:

- `params.offer`<!-- -->: Offer to inspect. Its market must be hydrated.

- `params.consumed`<!-- -->: Amount already consumed from the offer group.

- `params.timestamp`<!-- -->: Timestamp used to compute market time to maturity.

## Example


```ts
import { OfferUtils, midnightAbi } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";
import { createPublicClient, http } from "viem";
import { base } from "viem/chains";
import { readContract } from "viem/actions";

const client = createPublicClient({ chain: base, transport: http() });
const offer = {
  market: {
    params: {
      chainId: 8453,
      midnight: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001000",
      loanToken: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000006000",
      collateralParams: [
        {
          token: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000007000",
          lltv: 770000000000000000n,
          liquidationCursor: 250000000000000000n,
          oracle: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000008000",
        },
      ],
      maturity: 54_000n,
      rcfThreshold: 0n,
      enterGate: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000",
      liquidatorGate: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000",
    },
    totalUnits: 1_000n,
    lossFactor: 0n,
    withdrawable: 500n,
    continuousFeeCredit: 0n,
    settlementFeeCbps: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7],
    continuousFee: 10,
    tickSpacing: 4,
  },
  buy: true,
  maker: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000009000",
  start: 0n,
  expiry: 3_600n,
  tick: 5_000n,
  callback: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000",
  callbackData: "0x",
  receiverIfMakerIsSeller: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000",
  ratifier: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000004000",
  reduceOnly: false,
  maxUnits: 100n,
  maxAssets: 0n,
  continuousFeeCap: 317097919n,
} as const;
const consumed = await readContract(client, {
  address: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001000",
  abi: midnightAbi,
  functionName: "consumed",
  args: [offer.maker, "0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111111"],
});
const units = OfferUtils.getConsumableUnits({ offer, consumed, timestamp: 1_000n });
console.log(units);
```

```ts
  ratifier: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000004000",

});
```

<a name="midnight-sdk.payload"></a>

## Payload namespace

Midnight mempool payload codec namespace.

Use `Payload.encode` to turn ratified offer items into wire bytes for mempool publication or raw payload API validation, and `Payload.decode` to inspect published maker offers, ratifier data, or attribution-tagged payloads.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export declare namespace Payload
```

## Functions

<table><thead><tr><th>

Function


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

[decode(payload, options)](#midnight-sdk.payload.decode)


</td><td>

Parse a wire payload back into its `(offer, ratifierData)` items. The version byte is validated against `CURRENT_VERSION` and not surfaced — any payload that decodes successfully is on the current wire format. The 4-byte length prefix bounds the gzip stream; up to `MAX_ATTRIBUTION_SUFFIX_BYTES` bytes after it (e.g. an attribution suffix appended by the publishing app) are ignored, so a tagged payload decodes identically to an untagged one. A larger trailing suffix is rejected so an oversized blob cannot ride a small payload past validation and into the indexer.

Use on the take-side, in indexers, or in diagnostics when you need to inspect the offer structs and ratifier data that a maker published.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[encode(items)](#midnight-sdk.payload.encode)


</td><td>

ABI-encode `items` as `(Offer, bytes ratifierData)[]` and gzip the result, then emit the wire payload `version || uint32(gzipLen) || gzip(...)`<!-- -->. The single-byte version prefix lets future formats coexist on the wire; the 4-byte big-endian length delimits the gzip stream so `decode` finds its end without scanning. That delimiter is what lets a publisher append a small opaque suffix (e.g. an attribution tag) after the gzip stream — `decode` ignores up to `MAX_ATTRIBUTION_SUFFIX_BYTES` bytes past `gzipLen` and rejects a larger suffix. Item order is preserved verbatim and is the order a consumer sees on decode.

Use after ratifier utilities have produced payload-ready items and before an onchain mempool submission. Normal SDK maker flows should validate the tree with `Tree.mempoolValidate` before ratification; use `MidnightApi.validateMempoolPayload` only when validating already encoded payload bytes.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

## Variables

<table><thead><tr><th>

Variable


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

[CURRENT\_VERSION](#midnight-sdk.payload.current_version)


</td><td>

Current Midnight mempool payload wire version.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[MAX\_ATTRIBUTION\_SUFFIX\_BYTES](#midnight-sdk.payload.max_attribution_suffix_bytes)


</td><td>

Upper bound on opaque bytes appended after the gzip stream (e.g. an app attribution tag). The suffix is meant to be small, so `decode` rejects a larger one: this keeps the `MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES` ceiling meaningful for the whole input. Without it a tiny declared `gzipLen` could smuggle an arbitrarily large suffix past validation and into the indexer while still forcing the API to receive and hex-decode the whole blob.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[MAX\_COMPRESSED\_ITEMS\_BYTES](#midnight-sdk.payload.max_compressed_items_bytes)


</td><td>

Maximum gzip-compressed item bytes accepted by the payload codec.

The budget reserves room for the fixed header and the largest accepted attribution suffix so the full wire payload never exceeds .


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[MAX\_DECOMPRESSED\_ITEMS\_BYTES](#midnight-sdk.payload.max_decompressed_items_bytes)


</td><td>

Maximum ABI-decoded item bytes accepted by the payload codec.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[MAX\_PAYLOAD\_BYTES](#midnight-sdk.payload.max_payload_bytes)


</td><td>

Largest fully framed wire payload, in bytes, matching the router/onchain mempool cap.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[MAX\_PAYLOAD\_HEX\_LENGTH](#midnight-sdk.payload.max_payload_hex_length)


</td><td>

Largest `0x`<!-- -->-prefixed hex string that can encode a wire payload.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[MAX\_REQUEST\_BODY\_BYTES](#midnight-sdk.payload.max_request_body_bytes)


</td><td>

Largest inbound HTTP request body, in bytes, accepted by the API and gatekeeper APIs.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

## Type Aliases

<table><thead><tr><th>

Type Alias


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

[DecodeOptions](#midnight-sdk.payload.decodeoptions)


</td><td>

Optional decode bounds.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[Item](#midnight-sdk.payload.item)


</td><td>

One mempool payload item: a maker-side `Offer` together with the opaque `ratifierData` blob a taker hands to `Midnight.take(..., ratifierData)`<!-- -->.

`ratifierData` is owned by the ratifier scheme the maker used (e.g. `EcrecoverRatifierUtils.ratifierData`<!-- -->). The payload codec treats it as opaque bytes — simulators that only need to forward `ratifierData` can stay completely ratifier-agnostic.

Build items with `EcrecoverRatifierUtils.ratify` or `SetterRatifierUtils.ratify` after the tree is signed or approved, then pass the items to `Payload.encode` for publication.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

<a name="midnight-sdk.payload.decode"></a>

## Payload.decode() function

Parse a wire payload back into its `(offer, ratifierData)` items. The version byte is validated against `CURRENT_VERSION` and not surfaced — any payload that decodes successfully is on the current wire format. The 4-byte length prefix bounds the gzip stream; up to `MAX_ATTRIBUTION_SUFFIX_BYTES` bytes after it (e.g. an attribution suffix appended by the publishing app) are ignored, so a tagged payload decodes identically to an untagged one. A larger trailing suffix is rejected so an oversized blob cannot ride a small payload past validation and into the indexer.

Use on the take-side, in indexers, or in diagnostics when you need to inspect the offer structs and ratifier data that a maker published.

**Signature:**

```typescript
function decode(payload: Hex, options?: DecodeOptions): Promise<Item[]>;
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

payload


</td><td>

Hex


</td><td>

Hex payload bytes to decode.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

options


</td><td>

[DecodeOptions](#midnight-sdk.payload.decodeoptions)


</td><td>

_(Optional)_ Optional decode bounds.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

Promise&lt;[Item](#midnight-sdk.payload.item)<!-- -->\[\]&gt;

The decoded items in encoded order.

## Exceptions

`PayloadDecodeError` when the payload is malformed or exceeds protocol limits.

## Example


```ts
import { Offer, Payload } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";
import { zeroAddress } from "viem";

const offer = Offer.create({
  market: {
    chainId: 8453,
    midnight: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001000",
    loanToken: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000006000",
    collateralParams: [
      {
        token: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000007000",
        lltv: 770000000000000000n,
        liquidationCursor: 250000000000000000n,
        oracle: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000008000",
      },
    ],
    maturity: 54_000n,
    rcfThreshold: 0n,
    enterGate: zeroAddress,
    liquidatorGate: zeroAddress,
  },
  buy: true,
  maker: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000009000",
  tick: 5_000n,
  expiry: 3_600n,
  ratifier: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000004000",
  maxUnits: 100n,
});
const encoded = await Payload.encode([{ offer, ratifierData: "0x" }]);
const items = await Payload.decode(encoded);
console.log(items.length);
```

<a name="midnight-sdk.payload.encode"></a>

## Payload.encode() function

ABI-encode `items` as `(Offer, bytes ratifierData)[]` and gzip the result, then emit the wire payload `version || uint32(gzipLen) || gzip(...)`<!-- -->. The single-byte version prefix lets future formats coexist on the wire; the 4-byte big-endian length delimits the gzip stream so `decode` finds its end without scanning. That delimiter is what lets a publisher append a small opaque suffix (e.g. an attribution tag) after the gzip stream — `decode` ignores up to `MAX_ATTRIBUTION_SUFFIX_BYTES` bytes past `gzipLen` and rejects a larger suffix. Item order is preserved verbatim and is the order a consumer sees on decode.

Use after ratifier utilities have produced payload-ready items and before an onchain mempool submission. Normal SDK maker flows should validate the tree with `Tree.mempoolValidate` before ratification; use `MidnightApi.validateMempoolPayload` only when validating already encoded payload bytes.

**Signature:**

```typescript
function encode(items: readonly Item[]): Promise<Hex>;
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

items


</td><td>

readonly [Item](#midnight-sdk.payload.item)<!-- -->\[\]


</td><td>

Per-leaf items in the order the maker committed to. Must contain at least one item and fit within payload byte-size limits.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

Promise&lt;Hex&gt;

The encoded payload as a `Hex` string, ready to include in onchain mempool submission calldata.

## Exceptions

`PayloadDecodeError` when the item list is empty, encoding or compression exceeds SDK byte-size limits, or a non-empty offer fails payload validation for collateral requirements, maturity timing, expiry range, tick bounds, or `maxUnits`<!-- -->/`maxAssets` cap shape.

## Example


```ts
import { Offer, Payload } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";
import { zeroAddress } from "viem";

const offer = Offer.create({
  market: {
    chainId: 8453,
    midnight: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001000",
    loanToken: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000006000",
    collateralParams: [
      {
        token: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000007000",
        lltv: 770000000000000000n,
        liquidationCursor: 250000000000000000n,
        oracle: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000008000",
      },
    ],
    maturity: 54_000n,
    rcfThreshold: 0n,
    enterGate: zeroAddress,
    liquidatorGate: zeroAddress,
  },
  buy: true,
  maker: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000009000",
  tick: 5_000n,
  expiry: 3_600n,
  ratifier: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000004000",
  maxUnits: 100n,
});
const encoded = await Payload.encode([{ offer, ratifierData: "0x" }]);
console.log(encoded);
```

<a name="midnight-sdk.payload.item"></a>

## Payload.Item type

One mempool payload item: a maker-side `Offer` together with the opaque `ratifierData` blob a taker hands to `Midnight.take(..., ratifierData)`<!-- -->.

`ratifierData` is owned by the ratifier scheme the maker used (e.g. `EcrecoverRatifierUtils.ratifierData`<!-- -->). The payload codec treats it as opaque bytes — simulators that only need to forward `ratifierData` can stay completely ratifier-agnostic.

Build items with `EcrecoverRatifierUtils.ratify` or `SetterRatifierUtils.ratify` after the tree is signed or approved, then pass the items to `Payload.encode` for publication.

**Signature:**

```typescript
type Item = {
        readonly offer: IOffer;
        readonly ratifierData: Hex;
    };
```
**References:** [IOffer](#midnight-sdk.ioffer)

## Example


```ts
import { Offer, type Payload } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";
import { zeroAddress } from "viem";

const offer = Offer.create({
  market: {
    chainId: 8453,
    midnight: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001000",
    loanToken: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000006000",
    collateralParams: [
      {
        token: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000007000",
        lltv: 770000000000000000n,
        liquidationCursor: 250000000000000000n,
        oracle: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000008000",
      },
    ],
    maturity: 54_000n,
    rcfThreshold: 0n,
    enterGate: zeroAddress,
    liquidatorGate: zeroAddress,
  },
  buy: true,
  maker: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000009000",
  tick: 5_000n,
  expiry: 3_600n,
  ratifier: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000004000",
  maxUnits: 100n,
});
const item: Payload.Item = {
  offer,
  ratifierData: "0x",
};
console.log(item.ratifierData);
```

<a name="midnight-sdk.payload.max_attribution_suffix_bytes"></a>

## Payload.MAX\_ATTRIBUTION\_SUFFIX\_BYTES variable

Upper bound on opaque bytes appended after the gzip stream (e.g. an app attribution tag). The suffix is meant to be small, so `decode` rejects a larger one: this keeps the `MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES` ceiling meaningful for the whole input. Without it a tiny declared `gzipLen` could smuggle an arbitrarily large suffix past validation and into the indexer while still forcing the API to receive and hex-decode the whole blob.

**Signature:**

```typescript
MAX_ATTRIBUTION_SUFFIX_BYTES = 256
```

## Example


```ts
import { Payload } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";

console.log(Payload.MAX_ATTRIBUTION_SUFFIX_BYTES);
```

<a name="midnight-sdk.payload.max_compressed_items_bytes"></a>

## Payload.MAX\_COMPRESSED\_ITEMS\_BYTES variable

Maximum gzip-compressed item bytes accepted by the payload codec.

The budget reserves room for the fixed header and the largest accepted attribution suffix so the full wire payload never exceeds .

**Signature:**

```typescript
MAX_COMPRESSED_ITEMS_BYTES: number
```

```ts

console.log(Payload.MAX_COMPRESSED_ITEMS_BYTES);
```

<a name="midnight-sdk.ratifiertreeinput"></a>

## RatifierTreeInput type

Tree-like input accepted by ratifier helpers.

Pass a `Tree` or [TreeLike](#midnight-sdk.treelike) object to reuse cached hashes and proofs. Pass raw offer/group input when convenience matters more than avoiding a one-time tree materialization.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export type RatifierTreeInput = TreeLike | TreeInput;
```
**References:** [TreeLike](#midnight-sdk.treelike)<!-- -->, [TreeInput](#midnight-sdk.treeinput)

## Example


```ts
import { Offer, type RatifierTreeInput } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";
import { zeroAddress } from "viem";

const offer = Offer.create({
  market: {
    chainId: 8453,
    midnight: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001000",
    loanToken: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000006000",
    collateralParams: [
      {
        token: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000007000",
        lltv: 770000000000000000n,
        liquidationCursor: 250000000000000000n,
        oracle: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000008000",
      },
    ],
    maturity: 54_000n,
    rcfThreshold: 0n,
    enterGate: zeroAddress,
    liquidatorGate: zeroAddress,
  },
  buy: true,
  maker: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000009000",
  tick: 5_000n,
  expiry: 3_600n,
  ratifier: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000004000",
  maxUnits: 100n,
});
const tree: RatifierTreeInput = [offer];
console.log(tree);
```

<a name="midnight-sdk.ratifierutils"></a>

## RatifierUtils namespace

Utilities for selecting Midnight ratifier routes.

Call these during make-side preparation, before `Offer.create`<!-- -->, when an app must decide whether a maker can sign an Ecrecover root or must approve a Setter root onchain. Fetch helpers read bytecode for you; this namespace is the pure classification logic.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export declare namespace RatifierUtils
```

```ts
import { RatifierUtils } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";

console.log(RatifierUtils.isEip7702Designator("0xef0100"));
```

```typescript
function normalizeRatifierTree(params: {
        readonly tree: RatifierTreeInput;

    };
```

```ts
import { Offer, RatifierUtils } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";

    midnight: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001000",
    loanToken: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000006000",
    collateralParams: [
      {
        token: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000007000",
        lltv: 770000000000000000n,

      },
    ],
    maturity: 54_000n,
    rcfThreshold: 0n,
    enterGate: zeroAddress,
    liquidatorGate: zeroAddress,
  },
  buy: true,
  maker: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000009000",
  tick: 5_000n,
  expiry: 3_600n,
  ratifier: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000004000",
  maxUnits: 100n,
});
const { tree, ratifier } = RatifierUtils.normalizeRatifierTree({
  tree: [offer],
  label: "Ecrecover",
});
console.log(tree.root, ratifier);
```

```ts
    collateralParams: [
      {
        token: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000007000",
        lltv: 770000000000000000n,
        liquidationCursor: 250000000000000000n,
        oracle: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000008000",
      },
    ],
    maturity: 54_000n,
    rcfThreshold: 0n,
    enterGate: zeroAddress,

  buy: true,
  maker: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000009000",
  tick: 5_000n,
  expiry: 3_600n,
  ratifier: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000005000",

});

  tree: Tree.create([offer]),
```

<a name="midnight-sdk.setterratifierutils"></a>

## SetterRatifierUtils namespace

SetterRatifier-specific pure utilities.

Use this route for deployed-code makers. The make-side sequence is: create offers with the Setter ratifier address, build the group/tree, validate the tree, approve the root onchain for every maker in the tree, call `ratify`<!-- -->, then pass the returned items to `Payload.encode`<!-- -->. Ratifier helpers accept tree-like inputs rather than requiring the `Tree` class. Passing an existing `Tree` remains the optimal path because its cached offers, leaves, root, and height are reused when proofs are encoded.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export declare namespace SetterRatifierUtils
```

## Example


```ts
import { SetterRatifierUtils } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";

console.log(typeof SetterRatifierUtils.encodeRatifierData);
```

## Functions

<table><thead><tr><th>

Function


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

[decodeRatifierData(data)](#midnight-sdk.setterratifierutils.decoderatifierdata)


</td><td>

Decodes SetterRatifier ratifier data.

Use on the take-side or in tests after `Payload.decode` to inspect the proof attached to a published Setter offer.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[encodeRatifierData(params)](#midnight-sdk.setterratifierutils.encoderatifierdata)


</td><td>

Encodes SetterRatifier ratifier data.

Use only when you already have a root and proof. Most maker flows call `ratifierData` for one leaf or `ratify` for every leaf in the approved tree.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[ratifierData(params)](#midnight-sdk.setterratifierutils.ratifierdata)


</td><td>

Builds one ratifier-data value for a tree leaf.

Use after root approval when a caller needs data for one offer leaf. Use `ratify` to produce payload-ready items for the whole tree. Setter approvals are keyed by maker and root, so the maker for this leaf must have approved the tree root onchain.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[ratify(params)](#midnight-sdk.setterratifierutils.ratify)


</td><td>

Returns payload-ready items after a Setter root has been approved.

Use after `Tree.mempoolValidate` and the root approval transaction has been submitted for every maker in the tree. Setter approvals are keyed by maker and root, so mixed-maker trees need one approval per maker for the same root. The returned items can be passed directly to `Payload.encode`<!-- -->. All offers in the tree must use one ratifier address; build separate trees per ratifier.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[verifyRatifierData(params)](#midnight-sdk.setterratifierutils.verifyratifierdata)


</td><td>

Verifies that Setter ratifier data proves one payload offer belongs to its root.

This helper intentionally does not check `SetterRatifier.isRootRatified` or `Midnight.isAuthorized` state. Consumers can query those values at their own block context after local proof verification.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

<a name="midnight-sdk.setterratifierutils.ratify"></a>

## SetterRatifierUtils.ratify() function

Returns payload-ready items after a Setter root has been approved.

Use after `Tree.mempoolValidate` and the root approval transaction has been submitted for every maker in the tree. Setter approvals are keyed by maker and root, so mixed-maker trees need one approval per maker for the same root. The returned items can be passed directly to `Payload.encode`<!-- -->. All offers in the tree must use one ratifier address; build separate trees per ratifier.

**Signature:**

```typescript
function ratify(params: {
        readonly tree: RatifierTreeInput;
    }): readonly Payload.Item[];
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

params


</td><td>

{ readonly tree: [RatifierTreeInput](#midnight-sdk.ratifiertreeinput)<!-- -->; }


</td><td>


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

readonly [Payload.Item](#midnight-sdk.payload.item)<!-- -->\[\]

Items containing each offer and its ratifier data.

## Exceptions

`InvalidTreeError` when the tree is invalid or contains multiple ratifiers.

## Remarks

Parameter details:

- `params.tree`<!-- -->: Setter-ratified offer tree-like input whose root has already been approved onchain.

## Example


```ts
import { SetterRatifierUtils, Tree } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";
import { Offer } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";
import { zeroAddress } from "viem";

const offer = Offer.create({
  market: {
    chainId: 8453,
    midnight: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001000",
    loanToken: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000006000",
    collateralParams: [
      {
        token: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000007000",
        lltv: 770000000000000000n,
        liquidationCursor: 250000000000000000n,
        oracle: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000008000",
      },
    ],
    maturity: 54_000n,
    rcfThreshold: 0n,
    enterGate: zeroAddress,
    liquidatorGate: zeroAddress,
  },
  buy: true,
  maker: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000009000",
  tick: 5_000n,
  expiry: 3_600n,
  ratifier: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000005000",
  maxUnits: 100n,
});

const items = SetterRatifierUtils.ratify({
  tree: Tree.create([offer]),
});
console.log(items.length);
```

<a name="midnight-sdk.setterratifierutils.verifyratifierdata"></a>

## SetterRatifierUtils.verifyRatifierData() function

Verifies that Setter ratifier data proves one payload offer belongs to its root.

This helper intentionally does not check `SetterRatifier.isRootRatified` or `Midnight.isAuthorized` state. Consumers can query those values at their own block context after local proof verification.

**Signature:**

```typescript
function verifyRatifierData(params: SetterRatifierDataVerificationParams): DecodedSetterRatifierData;
```

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description

params


</td><td>

</td><td>


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

[DecodedSetterRatifierData](#midnight-sdk.decodedsetterratifierdata)

Decoded Setter ratifier data after proof verification.

## Exceptions

`InvalidTreeError` when the proof does not include `offer` in `root`<!-- -->.

## Remarks

Parameter details:

- `params.offer`<!-- -->: Offer carried by the payload item.

- `params.ratifierData`<!-- -->: ABI-encoded Setter ratifier data.

```ts
import { SetterRatifierUtils } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";

const decoded = SetterRatifierUtils.verifyRatifierData({
  offer,

```

<a name="midnight-sdk.takeamountslib.buyerassetstounits"></a>

## TakeAmountsLib.buyerAssetsToUnits() function

Converts a target buyer-asset amount into units for an offer.

`settlementFee` must be the fee for the offer market's current time to maturity.

**Signature:**

```typescript
function buyerAssetsToUnits(params: {
        readonly offer: {
            readonly buy: boolean;
            readonly tick: BigIntish;
        };
        readonly targetBuyerAssets: BigIntish;
        readonly settlementFee: BigIntish;
    }): bigint;
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

params


</td><td>

{ readonly offer: { readonly buy: boolean; readonly tick: [BigIntish](./morpho-ts.md#morpho-ts.bigintish)<!-- -->; }; readonly targetBuyerAssets: [BigIntish](./morpho-ts.md#morpho-ts.bigintish)<!-- -->; readonly settlementFee: [BigIntish](./morpho-ts.md#morpho-ts.bigintish)<!-- -->; }


</td><td>


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

bigint

Units that round-trip to the target buyer assets where reachable.

## Exceptions

`NegativeValueError` when `targetBuyerAssets`<!-- -->, `settlementFee`<!-- -->, or the offer tick is negative.

`DivisionByZeroError` when the computed buyer price is zero.

`PriceGreaterThanOneError` when buyer price is above WAD.

`TickOutOfRangeError` when the offer tick exceeds `MAX_TICK`<!-- -->.

`SettlementFeeExceedsPriceError` when settlement fee exceeds a buy offer price.

## Remarks

Parameter details:

- `params.offer.buy`<!-- -->: Whether the maker buys loan assets.

- `params.offer.tick`<!-- -->: Offer tick used to compute the buyer price.

- `params.targetBuyerAssets`<!-- -->: Target buyer-side asset amount.

- `params.settlementFee`<!-- -->: WAD-scaled settlement fee for the market and time to maturity.

## Example


```ts
import { TakeAmountsLib } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";

const offer = {
  buy: true,
  tick: 5_820n,
};

const units = TakeAmountsLib.buyerAssetsToUnits({
  offer,
  targetBuyerAssets: 100n,
  settlementFee: 0n,
});
console.log(units);
```

<a name="midnight-sdk.tree"></a>

## Tree class

Maker-side Merkle tree used by Midnight ratifiers.

Build a tree after offers have been created and related offers have been grouped. The tree root is what Ecrecover makers sign, Setter makers approve, and payload items later prove with per-leaf ratifier data.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export declare class Tree
```

## Example


```ts
import { Offer, Tree } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";
import { zeroAddress } from "viem";

const offer = Offer.create({
  market: {
    chainId: 8453,
    midnight: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001000",
    loanToken: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000006000",
    collateralParams: [
      {
        token: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000007000",
        lltv: 770000000000000000n,
        liquidationCursor: 250000000000000000n,
        oracle: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000008000",
      },
    ],
    maturity: 54_000n,
    rcfThreshold: 0n,
    enterGate: zeroAddress,
    liquidatorGate: zeroAddress,
  },
  buy: true,
  maker: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000009000",
  tick: 5_000n,
  expiry: 3_600n,
  ratifier: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000004000",
  maxUnits: 100n,
});
const tree = Tree.create([offer]);
console.log(tree.root);
```

<a name="midnight-sdk.tree.create"></a>

## Tree.create() method

Creates a tree from groups or standalone offers.

Use after `Offer.create` and optional `Group.create`<!-- -->, before `Tree.mempoolValidate`<!-- -->, `EcrecoverRatifierUtils.ratify`<!-- -->, or `SetterRatifierUtils.ratify`<!-- -->. Groups are flattened, and every standalone offer is normalized as a singleton group using the router-compatible group id algorithm.

**Signature:**

```typescript
static create(params: TreeCreateParams): Tree;
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

</th></tr></thead>

</td><td>

Groups or standalone offers in leaf order.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

[Tree](#midnight-sdk.tree)

Tree instance.

## Exceptions

`InvalidTreeError` when the tree is empty, all padding, or duplicated.

`InvalidTreeHeightError` when the resulting height is unsupported.

## Example


```ts
import { Offer, Tree } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";
import { zeroAddress } from "viem";

const offer = Offer.create({
  market: {
    chainId: 8453,
    midnight: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001000",
    loanToken: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000006000",
    collateralParams: [
      {
        token: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000007000",
        lltv: 770000000000000000n,
        liquidationCursor: 250000000000000000n,
        oracle: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000008000",
      },
    ],
    maturity: 54_000n,
    rcfThreshold: 0n,
    enterGate: zeroAddress,
    liquidatorGate: zeroAddress,
  },
  buy: true,
  maker: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000009000",
  tick: 5_000n,
  expiry: 3_600n,
  ratifier: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000004000",
  maxUnits: 100n,
});
const tree = Tree.create([offer]);
console.log(tree.height);
```

<a name="midnight-sdk.tree.mempoolvalidate"></a>

## Tree.mempoolValidate() method

Validates this tree against Midnight mempool API policy.

This is an API-backed convenience: by default it encodes each tree leaf with empty `ratifierData`<!-- -->, then sends the temporary payload to the Midnight API `POST /mempool/validate` endpoint. Pass `ratification` after signing or Setter root preparation to validate final payload bytes with real `ratifierData`<!-- -->.

**Signature:**

```typescript
mempoolValidate(params: TreeMempoolValidateParams): Promise<MempoolPayloadValidationSuccess>;
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

params


</td><td>

[TreeMempoolValidateParams](#midnight-sdk.treemempoolvalidateparams)


</td><td>


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

Promise&lt;MempoolPayloadValidationSuccess&gt;

Successful API validation result with `valid: true`<!-- -->.

## Exceptions

`PayloadDecodeError` when validation payload encoding fails.

`MidnightApiError` when the API returns a non-2xx response.

`InvalidMidnightApiResponseError` when the API returns malformed success JSON.

`MidnightMempoolValidationError` when the API returns validation issues.

## Remarks

Parameter details:

- `params.chainId`<!-- -->: Chain id whose API policy should validate this tree.

- `params.apiUrl`<!-- -->: Optional Midnight API URL override used for the validation HTTP request.

- `params.timestamp`<!-- -->: Optional ISO-8601 timestamp or `Date` selecting the API policy snapshot.

- `params.fetch`<!-- -->: Optional fetch implementation override used for the API call.

- `params.request`<!-- -->: Optional fetch options forwarded to the API request.

- `params.ratification`<!-- -->: Optional ratification inputs used to validate final payload bytes with real ratifier data.

## Example


```ts
import { Offer, Tree } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";
import { zeroAddress } from "viem";

const offer = Offer.create({
  market: {
    chainId: 8453,
    midnight: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001000",
    loanToken: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000006000",
    collateralParams: [
      {
        token: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000007000",
        lltv: 770000000000000000n,
        liquidationCursor: 250000000000000000n,
        oracle: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000008000",
      },
    ],
    maturity: 54_000n,
    rcfThreshold: 0n,
    enterGate: zeroAddress,
    liquidatorGate: zeroAddress,
  },
  buy: true,
  maker: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000009000",
  tick: 5_000n,
  expiry: 3_600n,
  ratifier: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000004000",
  maxUnits: 100n,
});
await Tree.create([offer]).mempoolValidate({
  chainId: 8453,
});
```

<a name="midnight-sdk.treecreateparams"></a>

## TreeCreateParams type

Entries accepted by [Tree.create()](#midnight-sdk.tree.create)<!-- -->.

Entries are either explicit groups or standalone offers. Explicit groups are flattened, and standalone offers are hashed with their own group ids.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export type TreeCreateParams = readonly GroupInput[];
```
**References:** [GroupInput](#midnight-sdk.groupinput)

## Example


```ts
import { Tree, type TreeCreateParams } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";
import { Offer } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";
import { zeroAddress } from "viem";

const offer = Offer.create({
  market: {
    chainId: 8453,
    midnight: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001000",
    loanToken: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000006000",
    collateralParams: [
      {
        token: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000007000",
        lltv: 770000000000000000n,
        liquidationCursor: 250000000000000000n,
        oracle: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000008000",
      },
    ],
    maturity: 54_000n,
    rcfThreshold: 0n,
    enterGate: zeroAddress,
    liquidatorGate: zeroAddress,
  },
  buy: true,
  maker: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000009000",
  tick: 5_000n,
  expiry: 3_600n,
  ratifier: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000004000",
  maxUnits: 100n,
});
const params = [offer] satisfies TreeCreateParams;
const tree = Tree.create(params);
console.log(tree.root);
```

## TreeDescriptor interface

Fully materialized tree descriptor.

Use this shape when a caller needs leaf structs, leaf hashes, root, and height without keeping a `Tree` instance, for example before custom signing or proof generation.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export interface TreeDescriptor
```

## Example


```ts
import { Offer, TreeUtils, type TreeDescriptor } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";
import { zeroAddress } from "viem";

const offer = Offer.create({
  market: {
    chainId: 8453,
    midnight: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001000",
    loanToken: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000006000",
    collateralParams: [
      {
        token: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000007000",
        lltv: 770000000000000000n,
        liquidationCursor: 250000000000000000n,
        oracle: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000008000",
      },
    ],
    maturity: 54_000n,
    rcfThreshold: 0n,
    enterGate: zeroAddress,
    liquidatorGate: zeroAddress,
  },
  buy: true,
  maker: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000009000",
  tick: 5_000n,
  expiry: 3_600n,
  ratifier: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000004000",
  maxUnits: 100n,
});
const tree: TreeDescriptor = TreeUtils.buildDescriptor([offer]);
console.log(tree.root);
```

<a name="midnight-sdk.treeinput"></a>

## TreeInput type

Plain creation input or class tree accepted by [Tree.from()](#midnight-sdk.tree.from)<!-- -->.

Use this only at boundaries that intentionally convert caller input into a `Tree`<!-- -->. Ratifier helpers accept [RatifierTreeInput](#midnight-sdk.ratifiertreeinput) instead, so they can reuse an existing `Tree` or normalize raw offer/group input.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export type TreeInput = Tree | TreeCreateParams | GroupInput;
```
**References:** [Tree](#midnight-sdk.tree)<!-- -->, [TreeCreateParams](#midnight-sdk.treecreateparams)<!-- -->, [GroupInput](#midnight-sdk.groupinput)

## Example


```ts
import { Offer, type TreeInput } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";
import { zeroAddress } from "viem";

const offer = Offer.create({
  market: {
    chainId: 8453,
    midnight: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001000",
    loanToken: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000006000",
    collateralParams: [
      {
        token: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000007000",
        lltv: 770000000000000000n,
        liquidationCursor: 250000000000000000n,
        oracle: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000008000",
      },
    ],
    maturity: 54_000n,
    rcfThreshold: 0n,
    enterGate: zeroAddress,
    liquidatorGate: zeroAddress,
  },
  buy: true,
  maker: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000009000",
  tick: 5_000n,
  expiry: 3_600n,
  ratifier: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000004000",
  maxUnits: 100n,
});
const tree: TreeInput = [offer];
console.log(tree);
```

<a name="midnight-sdk.treelike"></a>

## TreeLike interface

Tree-shaped data required by ratifier helpers.

A `Tree` class instance satisfies this shape and is the optimal input when a caller already built one, because the cached offers, leaves, root, and height are reused for signatures and proofs. Plain objects with these fields are also accepted by ratifier helpers.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export interface TreeLike
```

## Example


```ts
import { Offer, Tree, type TreeLike } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";
import { zeroAddress } from "viem";

const offer = Offer.create({
  market: {
    chainId: 8453,
    midnight: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001000",
    loanToken: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000006000",
    collateralParams: [
      {
        token: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000007000",
        lltv: 770000000000000000n,
        liquidationCursor: 250000000000000000n,
        oracle: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000008000",
      },
    ],
    maturity: 54_000n,
    rcfThreshold: 0n,
    enterGate: zeroAddress,
    liquidatorGate: zeroAddress,
  },
  buy: true,
  maker: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000009000",
  tick: 5_000n,
  expiry: 3_600n,
  ratifier: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000004000",
  maxUnits: 100n,
});
const tree: TreeLike = Tree.create([offer]);
console.log(tree.root);
```

<a name="midnight-sdk.treemempoolvalidateparams"></a>

## TreeMempoolValidateParams interface

Parameters for [Tree.mempoolValidate()](#midnight-sdk.tree.mempoolvalidate)<!-- -->.

Use this when an already-created tree should be validated by the Midnight API. By default it validates the pre-ratification tree with empty `ratifierData`<!-- -->; pass `ratification` to validate the final payload shape with real ratifier data.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export interface TreeMempoolValidateParams
```

## Example


```ts
import { Offer, Tree, type TreeMempoolValidateParams } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";
import { zeroAddress } from "viem";

const offer = Offer.create({
  market: {
    chainId: 8453,
    midnight: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001000",
    loanToken: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000006000",
    collateralParams: [
      {
        token: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000007000",
        lltv: 770000000000000000n,
        liquidationCursor: 250000000000000000n,
        oracle: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000008000",
      },
    ],
    maturity: 54_000n,
    rcfThreshold: 0n,
    enterGate: zeroAddress,
    liquidatorGate: zeroAddress,
  },
  buy: true,
  maker: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000009000",
  tick: 5_000n,
  expiry: 3_600n,
  ratifier: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000004000",
  maxUnits: 100n,
});
const tree = Tree.create([offer]);
const params = { chainId: 8453 } satisfies TreeMempoolValidateParams;
await tree.mempoolValidate(params);
```

<a name="midnight-sdk.treemempoolvalidateratification"></a>

## TreeMempoolValidateRatification type

Optional ratification inputs for [Tree.mempoolValidate()](#midnight-sdk.tree.mempoolvalidate)<!-- -->.

Omit this when validating offer policy before the maker signs or approves a tree. Provide it when validating the final payload shape, including real `ratifierData`<!-- -->, after the Ecrecover signature and signer address exist or the Setter root is ready for publication.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export type TreeMempoolValidateRatification = {
    readonly type: "ecrecover";
    readonly client: Client<Transport, Chain, Account | undefined>;
    readonly account: Account | Address;
    readonly signature?: undefined;
} | {
    readonly type: "ecrecover";
    readonly signature: EcrecoverSignatureInput;
    readonly account: Account | Address;
    readonly client?: undefined;
} | {
    readonly type: "setter";
};
```
**References:** [EcrecoverSignatureInput](#midnight-sdk.ecrecoversignatureinput)

## Example


```ts
import { zeroHash, type Signature } from "viem";
import type { TreeMempoolValidateRatification } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";

const ratification: TreeMempoolValidateRatification = {
  type: "ecrecover",
  account: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000009000",
  signature: { v: 27, r: zeroHash, s: zeroHash } satisfies Signature,
};
console.log(ratification.type);
```

```ts
      },

    maturity: 54_000n,
    rcfThreshold: 0n,
    enterGate: zeroAddress,
    liquidatorGate: zeroAddress,

  maker: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000009000",
  tick: 5_000n,
```

<a name="midnight-sdk.treeutils"></a>

## TreeUtils namespace

Object-compatible tree hashing, root, proof, and verification helpers.

Use these when you need pure tree hashing, descriptor construction, or proof verification. In the normal make-side flow, `Tree.create` wraps descriptor construction; proof helpers accept the built `Tree` so cached leaves/root are reused.

**Signature:**

```typescript
export declare namespace TreeUtils
```

## Example


```ts
import { TreeUtils } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";

console.log(typeof TreeUtils.buildRoot);
```

## Functions

<table><thead><tr><th>

Function


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

[buildDescriptor(entries)](#midnight-sdk.treeutils.builddescriptor)


</td><td>

Builds a tree descriptor and Merkle root. Non-power-of-two batches are padded with protocol-zero offers at the highest leaf indices.

Use after `Group.create` or standalone `Offer.create` when you need the padded leaves for custom signing, root approval, or proof construction. Groups are encoded with their derived shared group id, and standalone offers are encoded as singleton groups with the same algorithm. `Tree.create` calls this internally and is the simpler API for most make-side code.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[buildProof(params)](#midnight-sdk.treeutils.buildproof)


</td><td>

Builds a Merkle proof for one offer.

Use after tree construction when a custom ratifier needs one proof. The built-in Ecrecover and Setter helpers call this while generating `ratifierData`<!-- -->.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[buildRoot(entries)](#midnight-sdk.treeutils.buildroot)


</td><td>

Builds only the tree root.

Use when only the root is needed, for example to compare a locally built tree with an approved root. Use `Tree.create` or `buildDescriptor` if later proof generation is required.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[hashNode(left, right)](#midnight-sdk.treeutils.hashnode)


</td><td>

Computes HashLib node hash from left and right child hashes.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[mempoolValidate(params)](#midnight-sdk.treeutils.mempoolvalidate)


</td><td>

Validates a tree against Midnight mempool API policy.

This is an API-backed convenience: by default it encodes each tree leaf with empty `ratifierData`<!-- -->, then sends the temporary payload to the Midnight API `POST /mempool/validate` endpoint. Pass `ratification` after signing or Setter root preparation to validate final payload bytes with real `ratifierData`<!-- -->.


</td></tr>
<tr><td>

[verifyProof(params)](#midnight-sdk.treeutils.verifyproof)


</td><td>

Verifies a local Merkle proof against a root.

Use on the take-side or in tests to inspect decoded payload or ratifier data before forwarding it to a transaction builder. Onchain ratifiers still perform the authoritative verification.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

<a name="midnight-sdk.treeutils.builddescriptor"></a>

## TreeUtils.buildDescriptor() function

Builds a tree descriptor and Merkle root. Non-power-of-two batches are padded with protocol-zero offers at the highest leaf indices.

Use after `Group.create` or standalone `Offer.create` when you need the padded leaves for custom signing, root approval, or proof construction. Groups are encoded with their derived shared group id, and standalone offers are encoded as singleton groups with the same algorithm. `Tree.create` calls this internally and is the simpler API for most make-side code.

**Signature:**

```typescript
function buildDescriptor(entries: TreeCreateParams): TreeDescriptor;
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

entries


</td><td>

[TreeCreateParams](#midnight-sdk.treecreateparams)


</td><td>

Groups or standalone offers in leaf order.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

[TreeDescriptor](#midnight-sdk.treedescriptor)

Tree descriptor.

## Exceptions

`InvalidTreeError` when the offer count is empty, all padding, or duplicated.

`InvalidTreeHeightError` when the padded tree exceeds supported ratifier typehashes.

## Example


```ts
import { Offer, TreeUtils } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";
import { zeroAddress } from "viem";

const offer = Offer.create({
  market: {
    chainId: 8453,
    midnight: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001000",
    loanToken: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000006000",
    collateralParams: [
      {
        token: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000007000",
        lltv: 770000000000000000n,
        liquidationCursor: 250000000000000000n,
        oracle: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000008000",
      },
    ],
    maturity: 54_000n,
    rcfThreshold: 0n,
    enterGate: zeroAddress,
    liquidatorGate: zeroAddress,
  },
  buy: true,
  maker: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000009000",
  tick: 5_000n,
  expiry: 3_600n,
  ratifier: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000004000",
  maxUnits: 100n,
});
const tree = TreeUtils.buildDescriptor([offer]);
console.log(tree.root);
```

## TreeUtils.buildProof() function

Builds a Merkle proof for one offer.

Use after tree construction when a custom ratifier needs one proof. The built-in Ecrecover and Setter helpers call this while generating `ratifierData`<!-- -->.

**Signature:**

```typescript
function buildProof(params: {
        readonly tree: Pick<TreeLike, "leaves" | "root">;
```

## Example


```ts
import { Offer, Tree, TreeUtils } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";
import { zeroAddress } from "viem";

const offer = Offer.create({
  market: {
    chainId: 8453,
    midnight: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001000",
    loanToken: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000006000",
    collateralParams: [
      {
        token: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000007000",
        lltv: 770000000000000000n,
        liquidationCursor: 250000000000000000n,
        oracle: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000008000",
      },
    ],
    maturity: 54_000n,
    rcfThreshold: 0n,
    enterGate: zeroAddress,
    liquidatorGate: zeroAddress,
  },
  buy: true,
  maker: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000009000",
  tick: 5_000n,
  expiry: 3_600n,
  ratifier: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000004000",
  maxUnits: 100n,
});
const proof = TreeUtils.buildProof({
  tree: Tree.create([offer]),
  leafIndex: 0n,
});
console.log(proof.proof.length);
```

```ts
  maxUnits: 100n,
});
const root = TreeUtils.buildRoot([offer]);
console.log(root);
```

<a name="midnight-sdk.treeutils.mempoolvalidate"></a>

## TreeUtils.mempoolValidate() function

Validates a tree against Midnight mempool API policy.

This is an API-backed convenience: by default it encodes each tree leaf with empty `ratifierData`<!-- -->, then sends the temporary payload to the Midnight API `POST /mempool/validate` endpoint. Pass `ratification` after signing or Setter root preparation to validate final payload bytes with real `ratifierData`<!-- -->.

**Signature:**

```typescript
function mempoolValidate(params: Pick<TreeMempoolValidateParams, "chainId" | "apiUrl" | "timestamp" | "fetch" | "request"> & {
        readonly tree: TreeInput;
        readonly ratification?: TreeMempoolValidateRatification;
    }): Promise<MempoolPayloadValidationSuccess>;
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

params


</td><td>

Pick&lt;[TreeMempoolValidateParams](#midnight-sdk.treemempoolvalidateparams)<!-- -->, "chainId" \| "apiUrl" \| "timestamp" \| "fetch" \| "request"&gt; &amp; { readonly tree: [TreeInput](#midnight-sdk.treeinput)<!-- -->; readonly ratification?: [TreeMempoolValidateRatification](#midnight-sdk.treemempoolvalidateratification)<!-- -->; }


</td><td>


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

Promise&lt;MempoolPayloadValidationSuccess&gt;

Successful API validation result with `valid: true`<!-- -->.

## Exceptions

`InvalidTreeError` when the tree is empty, all padding, or duplicated.

`InvalidTreeHeightError` when the resulting height is unsupported.

`PayloadDecodeError` when validation payload encoding fails.

`MidnightApiError` when the API returns a non-2xx response.

`InvalidMidnightApiResponseError` when the API returns malformed success JSON.

`MidnightMempoolValidationError` when the API returns validation issues.

## Remarks

Parameter details:

- `params.chainId`<!-- -->: Chain id whose API policy should validate the tree.

- `params.tree`<!-- -->: Offer tree to validate.

- `params.apiUrl`<!-- -->: Optional Midnight API URL override used for the validation HTTP request.

- `params.timestamp`<!-- -->: Optional ISO-8601 timestamp or `Date` selecting the API policy snapshot.

- `params.fetch`<!-- -->: Optional fetch implementation override used for the API call.

- `params.request`<!-- -->: Optional fetch options forwarded to the API request.

- `params.ratification`<!-- -->: Optional ratification inputs used to validate final payload bytes with real ratifier data.

## Example


```ts
import { Offer, TreeUtils } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";
import { zeroAddress } from "viem";

const offer = Offer.create({
  market: {
    chainId: 8453,
    midnight: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001000",
    loanToken: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000006000",
    collateralParams: [
      {
        token: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000007000",
        lltv: 770000000000000000n,
        liquidationCursor: 250000000000000000n,
        oracle: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000008000",
      },
    ],
    maturity: 54_000n,
    rcfThreshold: 0n,
    enterGate: zeroAddress,
    liquidatorGate: zeroAddress,
  },
  buy: true,
  maker: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000009000",
  tick: 5_000n,
  expiry: 3_600n,
  ratifier: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000004000",
  maxUnits: 100n,
});
await TreeUtils.mempoolValidate({
  chainId: 8453,
  tree: [offer],
});
```

<a name="midnight-sdk.treeutils.verifyproof"></a>

## TreeUtils.verifyProof() function

Verifies a local Merkle proof against a root.

Use on the take-side or in tests to inspect decoded payload or ratifier data before forwarding it to a transaction builder. Onchain ratifiers still perform the authoritative verification.

**Signature:**

```typescript
function verifyProof(params: {
        readonly offer: IOffer;
        readonly root: Hash;
        readonly leafIndex: BigIntish;
        readonly proof: readonly Hash[];
    }): boolean;
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

Description


</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

params


</td><td>

{ readonly offer: [IOffer](#midnight-sdk.ioffer)<!-- -->; readonly root: Hash; readonly leafIndex: [BigIntish](./morpho-ts.md#morpho-ts.bigintish)<!-- -->; readonly proof: readonly Hash\[\]; }


</td><td>


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

boolean

Whether the proof reconstructs the supplied root.

## Remarks

Parameter details:

- `params.offer`<!-- -->: Offer whose hash starts proof reconstruction.

- `params.root`<!-- -->: Expected Merkle root.

- `params.leafIndex`<!-- -->: Leaf index proven by `params.proof`<!-- -->.

- `params.proof`<!-- -->: Merkle proof siblings for the leaf.

## Example


```ts
import { Offer, Tree, TreeUtils } from "@morpho-org/midnight-sdk";
import { zeroAddress } from "viem";

const offer = Offer.create({
  market: {
    chainId: 8453,
    midnight: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001000",
    loanToken: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000006000",
    collateralParams: [
      {
        token: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000007000",
        lltv: 770000000000000000n,
        liquidationCursor: 250000000000000000n,
        oracle: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000008000",
      },
    ],
    maturity: 54_000n,
    rcfThreshold: 0n,
    enterGate: zeroAddress,
    liquidatorGate: zeroAddress,
  },
  buy: true,
  maker: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000009000",
  tick: 5_000n,
  expiry: 3_600n,
  ratifier: "0x0000000000000000000000000000000000004000",
  maxUnits: 100n,
});
const tree = Tree.create([offer]);
const proof = tree.proof(0n);
const valid = TreeUtils.verifyProof({
  offer: tree.offers[0]!,
  root: proof.root,
  leafIndex: proof.leafIndex,
  proof: proof.proof,
});
console.log(valid);
```
